segmentation.text: A person shall not drive a motor vehicle
at a speed in excess of 15 miles per hour
in an area designated as a school zone
except:
(a) On a day on which school is not in session;
(b) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(c) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or (d) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

As used in this section, “speed limit beacon” means a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit in a school zone or school crossing zone is in effect.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle for 'motor vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-130: 'every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); it is claimed as the aggregate and never expanded into classes. 'A person shall not drive' names no class: who drives is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency), so the exclusion 'a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle — never membership' does not apply: the aggregate carries only the vehicle's class.

kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity' (m/s). 'at a speed in excess of' compares the subject's speed with the figure the law states, carried as a literal (s2); the speed is a state at each observation, so the comparison is read at the judged observation. No 'not a stand-in for' clause of the contract applies.

dev.zone_sign: 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}; end attribute'. Ontology §9: 'Where the same category is also marked on the road by a sign (dev.zone_sign), the sign is the atom and the category is not.' The school zone (DEF-NRS-484B-063: 'those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property') is that category; 'an area designated as a school zone' is the stretch a zone sign z of kind school, not an end sign, governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'), read over st.travel_region, the kind dev.governs ranges over; the subject is in it where its footprint overlaps such a region r (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold', which this node reads only in exception (d); dev.governs is 'not a stand-in for a position' and no halt place is read from it. 'designated' is the legal status of the sign, read by its presence (observable_reading status).

dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect', the device the section defines (s12). The zone is designated by a beacon b where b governs the zone's region r (dev.governs over st.travel_region). 'operational' is read as b not inoperative: dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', applies to the beacon's head of lamps, so a beacon present and not inoperative is operational. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: no place is read from it.

dev.speed_limit_beacon carries a 'flashing attribute': its lamps flash 'alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. 'the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect' is that attribute false for every operational beacon that governs r (the beacon of exception (c)).

The negation of s7: no dev.speed_limit_beacon ('a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign') that governs r (dev.governs, over st.travel_region) is present and not inoperative (dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'). An inoperative beacon leaves the zone 'not designated by an operational speed limit beacon'.

dev.zone_sign's 'conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend — a list of time windows ...; a legend read with no restriction is the empty set (unconditional), a legend not read is absent (every condition unknown)'. prim.conditions_hold: 'the structured conditions of a device (dev.zone_sign, dev.regulatory_sign) hold at the observation for a road user'. 'the sign designating the school zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect' is prim.conditions_hold false for z, the sign of s3, and the subject. dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold', which is why the primitive is read; its input env.civil_time is the primitive's own.

The section's definition of 'speed limit beacon' ('a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit ... is in effect') is the contract of dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. It adds no condition beyond the atom's, and the beacon is read as that atom in s7, s9 and s10.

assumptions.meaning: the date of the observation is a day on which the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place is in session, as the reading declares from that school's calendar

the time of the observation lies in the period from a half hour after the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place ceased operation to a half hour before that school next begins operation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule
the pupils of the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place are in class at the time of the observation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule

applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle). At the judged observation its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region r that a dev.zone_sign z of kind school, not an end sign, governs (dev.governs); and, for that z and r, none of these holds at the judged observation: (a) asm.school_in_session_day is false; (b) asm.school_outside_operation_margin holds; (c) some dev.speed_limit_beacon governs r and is not dev.inoperative, asm.pupils_in_class holds, and no dev.speed_limit_beacon that governs r and is not inoperative is flashing; (d) no dev.speed_limit_beacon that governs r is present and not inoperative, and prim.conditions_hold for z and the subject is false. 'designated' is the legal status of the zone: the zone sign governing the subject's region is the evidence, and the school property the zone adjoins is not read.

shall not make a U-turn
in an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone
except:
(a) When there are no children present;
(b) On a day on which school is not in session;
(c) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(d) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or (e) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation is one at which drv.motion.u_turn(subject; window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) holds, i.e. the U-turn's recognition. The U-turn is under way at the observations of the window behind (p.vehicle_turn_window) at which the subject's kin.yaw_rate exceeds p.turn_yaw_rate_tol in magnitude. The duty applies where, at some observation while the U-turn is under way, the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.zone_sign z of kind school or school_crossing that is not an end sign, and, for that z and r, none of the exceptions holds at every observation while the U-turn is under way: (a) no ru.child lies within p.pedestrian_near_reach (st.region_geometry distance) of any travel region z governs; (b) asm.school_in_session_day is false; (c) asm.school_outside_operation_margin holds; (d) some dev.speed_limit_beacon governs r and is not dev.inoperative, asm.pupils_in_class holds, and no beacon that governs r and is not inoperative is flashing; (e) no beacon that governs r is present and not inoperative, and prim.conditions_hold for z and the subject is false. Each exception is read as a whole at each observation (its spans joined by 'and' at the same moment) and excuses the act only where it holds at every observation while the act is under way.
obligation: drv.motion.u_turn(subject) with window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min and yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol does not hold at the judged observation: a recognized U-turn in the zone violates the duty. Where the window behind is truncated or a yaw rate in it is missing, the concept and the occasion are unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver' and 'make' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
'designated' is the legal status of the zone: the zone sign governing the subject's region is the evidence.

under_way.words: the observations of the window behind the recognition at which the subject's heading is turning
under_way.justification: kin.yaw_rate: 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left'. drv.motion.u_turn is recognized where 'the heading has stopped turning'; the observations of its window at which the yaw rate magnitude exceeds p.turn_yaw_rate_tol (the concept's own yaw_tol) are those at which the reversal is being made, which tells them from the straight travel before the act began. 'Not a stand-in for road curvature — a vehicle yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres' is the reason it marks the manoeuvre and not the road.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not overtake and pass another vehicle traveling in the same direction
in an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone
except:
(a) On a day on which the school is not in session;
(b) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(c) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or (d) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

As used in this section, “speed limit beacon” means a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit in a school zone or school crossing zone is in effect.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for 'vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power ...'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the aggregate carries only the class.

drv.interaction.overtake_pass: 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it', recognized when b comes to be behind a after b was ahead with headings aligned within same_dir_cos. 'overtake and pass another vehicle traveling in the same direction' is that act with a the subject and b any other road user of the scene that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the admitted aggregate of 'vehicle', 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'); the concept's aligned headings carry 'in the same direction'. The concept 'says nothing ... of whether b moves', so 'traveling' is carried beside it: b's kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance at some observation while the pass is under way, so a pass of a vehicle at rest throughout is not this duty. b is quantified in the rule, not a binder.

dev.zone_sign: 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}; end attribute'. Ontology §9: 'Where the same category is also marked on the road by a sign (dev.zone_sign), the sign is the atom and the category is not.' The school zone (DEF-NRS-484B-063: 'those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property') and the school crossing zone (DEF-NRS-484B-060: 'those sections of streets not adjacent to school property that pupils cross while following a designated walking route to school') are those categories; the area designated as either is the stretch a zone sign z of kind school or school_crossing, not an end sign, governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', over st.travel_region); the pass is made in it where, while the pass is under way, the subject's footprint overlaps such a region r (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold', read only in exception (d); dev.governs is 'not a stand-in for a position'. 'designated' is read by the sign's presence (observable_reading status).

dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect', the device the section defines (s12). The zone is designated by a beacon b where b governs the zone's region r (dev.governs over st.travel_region). 'operational' is read as b not inoperative: dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', applies to the beacon's head of lamps. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position.

dev.speed_limit_beacon carries a 'flashing attribute': its lamps flash 'alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. 'not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect' is that attribute false for every operational beacon that governs r.

The negation of s7: no dev.speed_limit_beacon ('a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign') that governs r (dev.governs, over st.travel_region) is present and not inoperative (dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication').

dev.zone_sign's 'conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend' and prim.conditions_hold: 'the structured conditions of a device (dev.zone_sign, dev.regulatory_sign) hold at the observation for a road user'. 'the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect' is prim.conditions_hold false for z, the sign of s3, and the subject. dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold'; env.civil_time is the primitive's own input.

The section's definition of 'speed limit beacon' ('a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit ... is in effect') is the contract of dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. It adds no condition beyond the atom's.

assumptions.meaning: the date of the observation is a day on which the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place is in session, as the reading declares from that school's calendar

the time of the observation lies in the period from a half hour after the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place ceased operation to a half hour before that school next begins operation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule
the pupils of the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place are in class at the time of the observation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). For each other road user b of the scene that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same(b, subject) excluded), the pass of b is the act drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b; window p.overtake_window, same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos), recognized at the observation at which it holds; it is under way from the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction within p.overtake_same_direction_cos) up to the recognition. The duty applies to that pass where b's kin.speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance at some observation while the pass is under way, and where, at some observation while the pass is under way, the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.zone_sign z of kind school or school_crossing, not an end sign, and, for that z and r, none of the exceptions holds at every observation while the pass is under way: (a) asm.school_in_session_day is false; (b) asm.school_outside_operation_margin holds; (c) some dev.speed_limit_beacon governs r and is not dev.inoperative, asm.pupils_in_class holds, and no beacon that governs r and is not inoperative is flashing; (d) no beacon that governs r is present and not inoperative, and prim.conditions_hold for z and the subject is false. With no other vehicle in the scene the duty is met.
obligation: For every such b, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b) with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos does not hold at the judged observation: a recognized pass of a travelling vehicle in the zone violates the duty. Where the window behind is truncated or b's bearing or overlap is unobserved, the pass and its occasion are unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver' and 'overtake' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
'designated' is the legal status of the zone: the zone sign governing the subject's region is the evidence.

under_way.words: from the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the moving subject with headings aligned, up to the recognition
under_way.justification: drv.interaction.overtake_pass: 'The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction)', where 'b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative)'. segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection and:
The turn is a right turn,
both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane
if the highway has a right turn lane
as set forth in subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b],
or must be made from the extreme right lane.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for 'vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power ...'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the aggregate carries only the class.

st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges' (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of two highways which join one another'); the intersection i is the target region of the declared intention and the region whose entry ends the approach: the subject enters i at the observation e at which its footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') having not overlapped it at the observation before. Its approach is 'a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection' (st.lane_enters: 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), the carriers being lanes (st.lane) or the kinds refining them. st.intersection is 'not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line': no halt place is read. st.lane_enters is 'not a stand-in for ... the subject's presence in the intersection', which rel.occupies reads.

st.turn_lane: 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}'; the right turn lane of the approach is the turn lane t of side right that enters i (st.lane_enters) and that s6 selects. 'the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane': the approach ends and the turn begins at the subject's entry into i, and at the observation before that entry the subject's footprint overlaps t (rel.occupies). st.turn_lane refines st.lane, whose exclusion 'a half of the roadway or a lateral position within a lane' does not apply: lane membership is read by occupancy. The approach is read at its end and the turn at its start (narrowing disclosed): a lane change into t earlier on the approach is not a breach.

The words borrow subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223, which quotes: 'If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning'. The highway the subject approaches on has such a lane where exactly one st.turn_lane ('a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}') of side right enters i (st.lane_enters) and its designated direction (st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') is aligned with that of a lane the subject occupies entering i, the cosine of the angle between the two directions at or above p.approach_lane_same_direction_cos; turn lanes of other approaches to i point along other legs and are not the subject's highway's. 'single' is kept: a second such lane makes the condition false. 'used only for turning' is the turn lane's own kind. st.lane_direction is read normalised, as its contract says.

compositions.quote: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: 'as set forth in subsection 4' borrows only that subsection's description of the lane: a single right lane, provided by the highway's design, used only for turning (kept in s6 as exactly one right turn lane of the approach). Whether a right turn lane exists is a fact of the road, not a verdict: the lane is the right turn lane whether or not any vehicle in it complies with the subsection's duty to be driven there only to turn right, so that rule need not apply, hold or be complied with here.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation e is one at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies) and did not at the observation before (its entry). int.right_turn(subject, i) is declared true at the observation before e (the intention to turn, and the turn being a right turn, s2 and s4). At the observation before e the subject occupies a lane c that enters i (st.lane_enters c i), and there is exactly one st.turn_lane t of side right that enters i whose designated direction (st.lane_direction) makes with c's a cosine at or above p.approach_lane_same_direction_cos (the highway has a right turn lane, s6 with s7). Whether the event occurred is unknown where the observation before e does not show the subject's place (the subject's first observation, or no mapped carrier); a missing direction, kind or entrance makes the applicability unknown only where the verdict turns on it.
obligation: At the observation before e, the subject's footprint overlaps the right turn lane t (rel.occupies): the approach ends and the right turn is begun from t. Where the subject at the observation before e occupies t, the duty is met whatever else is unobserved; where it occupies no lane entering i that could be t, it is violated; where t's identity turns on an unobserved direction, it is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

'the approach for the right turn and the right turn' are read at the observation before the entry into the intersection, where the approach ends and the turn begins: the subject must then be in the right turn lane. A lane change into it earlier on the approach is not a breach, and the turn is identified by the declared intention and the entry, not by a recognized heading change.

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection and:
Both intersecting highways are two-directional:
The approach for a left turn must be made in that portion of the right half of the highway nearest the centerline thereof.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for 'vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power ...'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the aggregate carries only the class.

st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges' (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of two highways which join one another'); i is the target region of the declared intention and the region whose entry ends the approach: the subject enters i at the observation e at which its footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') having not overlapped it at the observation before. Its approach is a carrier it occupies whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters: 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'): a lane (st.lane) or a roadway recorded as a directed approach segment (st.roadway). st.intersection is 'not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line'; st.lane_enters is 'not a stand-in for ... the subject's presence in the intersection'.

'two-directional' uses DEF-NRS-484B-073: 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions'. The intersecting highways are the highways i lies on (st.on_way: 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there'; st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'). 'undivided' is read with DEF-NRS-484A-070 ('divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section'): no st.median_or_divider ('physical barrier or dividing section between roadways') lies on h. 'allowed to proceed in opposite directions' is two carriers lying on h (lanes or roadway directed segments) whose designated directions (st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') are opposed, the cosine at or below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos. 'Both' is every highway i lies on. st.on_way is 'not a stand-in for nearness to a way': no distance is read.

'centerline' uses DEF-NRS-484A-040: 'a continuous or broken line marked upon the surface of a highway by paint or otherwise to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions'; the right half is therefore the carriers allocated to the subject's direction, and the side of the centerline is read by designated directions (st.lane_direction), not by a lane ordinal alone (st.lane: 'lane ordinal equals roadway half only on a two-lane road'). 'The approach for a left turn' is the approach that ends at the subject's entry into i: at the observation before entry the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a carrier c entering i (st.lane_enters). 'that portion of the right half ... nearest the centerline' is the lane of the subject's direction next to the centerline: st.lane_adjacency, 'ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction'; where the subject occupies no lane entering i, a roadway directed approach segment entering i (st.roadway) carries a single line of traffic, itself that portion. 'in ... the right half' is also the subject occupying no lane or roadway segment lying on the same way as c (st.on_way, st.highway) whose designated direction is opposed to c's (cosine at or below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos). st.lane_adjacency is 'not a stand-in for the marking between two lanes'.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation e is one at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies) and did not at the observation before (its entry). int.left_turn(subject, i) is declared true at the observation before e (s2; the turn is the left turn s5 names). Every highway h that i lies on (st.on_way i h) is two-directional: no st.median_or_divider lies on h, and two lanes or roadway segments lying on h carry designated directions (st.lane_direction) whose cosine is at or below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos. Whether the entry occurred is unknown where the observation before e does not show the subject's place.
obligation: At the observation before e the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a carrier c entering i (st.lane_enters c i) that is the portion of the right half nearest the centerline: a lane of st.lane_adjacency ordinal 1, or, where the subject occupies no lane entering i, a roadway directed approach segment entering i; and the subject occupies no lane or roadway segment lying on the same highway as c (st.on_way) whose designated direction makes with c's a cosine at or below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos. Approaching only in a lane of higher ordinal, or with the footprint over an opposing carrier, violates the duty; an unobserved ordinal or direction makes it unknown where the verdict turns on it.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

'The approach' is read at its end, the observation before the entry into the intersection; 'that portion ... nearest the centerline' is read at the granularity of lanes: the lane of the subject's direction next to the centerline, and, on an approach with a single line of traffic, that whole line. A lateral position within the lane is not read.

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection and:
Both intersecting highways are two-directional:
After entering the intersection, the left turn must be made so as to leave the intersection to the right of the centerline of the highway being entered.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for 'vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power ...'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the aggregate carries only the class.

st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges' (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of two highways which join one another'); i is the target region of the declared intention and the region the left turn is made through: the subject's footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') from its entry to its exit. st.intersection is 'not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line': no halt place is read.

'two-directional' uses DEF-NRS-484B-073: 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions'. The intersecting highways are the highways i lies on (st.on_way: 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there'; st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'). 'undivided' is read with DEF-NRS-484A-070 ('divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section'): no st.median_or_divider ('physical barrier or dividing section between roadways') lies on h. 'allowed to proceed in opposite directions' is two carriers lying on h (lanes or roadway directed segments) whose designated directions (st.lane_direction) are opposed, the cosine at or below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos. 'Both' is every highway i lies on. st.on_way is 'not a stand-in for nearness to a way'.

drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(subject, i): 'Road user a has made a turn to the left through region r, recognized as it leaves r. The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies) ... its entry into r. The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r.' 'After entering the intersection, the left turn must be made so as to leave the intersection' is that act, begun at the entry and recognized at the exit. 'to the right of the centerline of the highway being entered': DEF-NRS-484A-040 makes the centerline the line 'to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions', so the subject leaves to its right where, at the exit, it moves against the designated direction of no lane its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies over st.lane): drv.motion.moving_against_carrier(subject, l): 'part of its motion runs opposite to r's designated direction', with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, is false for every such lane l. The lanes the subject overlaps at the exit lie on the highway it enters. moving_against_carrier 'says nothing of whether a occupies r', which rel.occupies supplies.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation is the recognition of drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(subject, i; step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min) for an intersection i (st.intersection): the subject's exit from i after its entry, its heading change since the entry in the left-turn band. The act is under way from the entry into i (rel.occupies rising) up to the exit. int.left_turn(subject, i) is declared true at some observation while the act is under way (read behind the judged observation). i is the act's region and its kind is read at the recognition. Every highway h that i lies on (st.on_way i h) is two-directional, read at the recognition: no st.median_or_divider lies on h, and two lanes or roadway segments lying on h carry designated directions whose cosine is at or below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos.
obligation: At the recognition (the exit from i), for every st.lane l the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), drv.motion.moving_against_carrier(subject, l; speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) is false: the subject leaves the intersection in lanes allocated to its own direction, to the right of the centerline of the highway entered. A lane overlapped against its direction violates the duty; an unobserved lane direction or velocity makes it unknown where the verdict turns on it. Where the entry lies before the recording or a yaw rate since the entry is missing, the act is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

'to the right of the centerline of the highway being entered' is read through the lanes the subject overlaps as it leaves the intersection: none may carry a designated direction its motion runs against. A highway entered with no mapped lane is not read here.

onset.justification: drv.motion.left_turn_through_region: 'The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r.' r is the intersection i (st.intersection).

occasion.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r.

under_way.words: the observations from the subject's entry into the intersection up to its exit, at which it is moving through it and turning
under_way.justification: rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region': the subject did not overlap i before its entry, so overlap since the entry, together with the heading change integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading') since that entry, tells an observation inside the turn from one on the approach before it began.

segmentation.text: If an official traffic-control device indicates that a U-turn is prohibited,
the driver
shall obey the directions of the device.

elements.justification: 'official traffic-control device' uses DEF-NRS-484A-145: 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'. The law's own words 'indicates that a U-turn is prohibited' limit it to the members whose indication is that prohibition: dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code ... no_u_turn ...', with code no_u_turn; a signal's arrows indicate stop or go, not a U-turn prohibition, and no marking of the ontology states one (disclosed in PLAN.md). The sign's 'conditions attribute ... read as that row says (unconditional when empty, unknown when absent)' is read through prim.conditions_hold ('the structured conditions of a device (dev.zone_sign, dev.regulatory_sign) hold at the observation for a road user'): the sign indicates the prohibition while its conditions hold. The sign directs the traffic of the travel regions it governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', over st.travel_region): the subject is under it where its footprint overlaps such a region (rel.occupies), or overlaps an intersection (st.intersection) that a governed lane (st.lane) enters (st.lane_enters: 'a device governs a lane and the lane enters an intersection; which intersection a device controls is read through both') having entered that intersection from that lane. dev.regulatory_sign is 'not a stand-in for a manoeuvre': the U-turn is read by its concept (s3). 'official' is read by the sign's presence (observable_reading status).

'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the class it presupposes is the vehicle of that definition's words, carried by the run's admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), claimed as the aggregate and never expanded. The exclusion 'a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle — never membership' does not apply: the aggregate carries the vehicle's class only.

drv.motion.u_turn (definition DEF-NRS-484B-077): 'Road user a has turned “so as to proceed in the opposite direction”: its heading has reversed, “whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not”'. The direction of a no-U-turn sign is that no U-turn be made under it: 'obey the directions of the device' is the subject making no U-turn (the concept not holding at its recognition) where the sign governs it while the U-turn is under way. The concept 'says nothing of the way on which a turns', which s1 supplies.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation is one at which drv.motion.u_turn(subject; window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) holds, i.e. a U-turn's recognition; the U-turn is under way at the observations of the window behind at which the subject's kin.yaw_rate exceeds p.turn_yaw_rate_tol in magnitude. The duty applies where, at some observation while the U-turn is under way, a dev.regulatory_sign s of code no_u_turn whose conditions hold for the subject there (prim.conditions_hold) governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), or governs a lane l that enters (st.lane_enters) an intersection the subject's footprint overlaps, the subject having occupied l at the observation before it entered that intersection.
obligation: drv.motion.u_turn(subject) with window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min and yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol does not hold at the judged observation: a U-turn made under a no-U-turn sign disobeys it. Where the window is truncated or a yaw rate in it is missing, the concept and its occasion are unknown.

narrowings.why: 'official' is the legal status of the sign: the no-U-turn sign present and governing the subject's region is the evidence.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
'obey the directions of the device' is read as making no U-turn under it: the only direction a no-U-turn sign gives.

under_way.words: the observations of the window behind the recognition at which the subject's heading is turning
under_way.justification: kin.yaw_rate: 'rate of change of heading'. drv.motion.u_turn is recognized where 'the heading has stopped turning'; the observations of its window at which the yaw-rate magnitude exceeds p.turn_yaw_rate_tol (the concept's own yaw_tol) are those at which the reversal is being made, which tells them from travel before it began; 'not a stand-in for road curvature — a vehicle yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres'.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.regulatory_sign of code no_u_turn with empty conditions governs the subject's approach lane; the subject begins turning in that lane, enters the intersection and reverses its heading (heading change in the reversal band, then yaw below tolerance).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same sign and lane; the subject drives straight through the intersection: no U-turn is recognized.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject makes a U-turn on a lane no no_u_turn sign governs; no sign governs the intersection or a lane entering it from which the subject came.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid, but the source declares kin.yaw_rate absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The no_u_turn sign's conditions state hours that do not include the time of the observation (prim.conditions_hold false throughout the U-turn); the subject makes the U-turn under it.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1
scenarios.narrative: The no_u_turn sign governs the lane the subject occupies as it begins turning; the subject completes the reversal on lanes the sign does not govern, so that the governed lane is overlapped only at the first observations while the U-turn is under way.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1_outside
